documents.own_summary: Choose the activity before choosing hardware or packages. A browser is enough to read; small local experiments use the uv-managed .venv CPU/GPU toolbox; the photo/speech assistant uses a separately pinned .venv-natural. Verify basic computation separately from answer quality, and acquire only the data/model artifacts the chosen activity needs.

own_workflow_explanation.roles: Browser-only reader needs no installation. A short-experiment reader opens the selected course Notebook in Colab or uses .venv locally. A small-model training reader follows the separate training route after learning the concept. A Chapter 20 user loads two pretrained models, a Qwen3-VL image/text assistant and a Whisper recognizer; spoken audio becomes text before chat, and the answer is text. A maintainer keeps fixed source/data/model identities and publishes their entry points. LoRA candidates are optional corrections beside the full base; the selected student configuration says it uses the base with no added correction.
own_workflow_explanation.counts_and_numbers: Two environments are alternatives for different project workflows, not two model copies. Three small-model extras (cpu/cu126/cu130) are mutually exclusive package choices; 12.6/13.0 describe CUDA compatibility, and the Chapter 20 environment separately uses CUDA 12.8 or CPU with Python 3.12/PyTorch 2.8.0. The storage table describes eight initial source packages totaling 30,854,837 bytes (~30.85 decimal MB) and three Chapter 20 packages totaling 146,543,309 bytes (~146.54 MB). The first supports 30 formal experiments, which is not a claim of 30 distinct pretrained assistants. DATA separately reports 2,077/124/170 text-image training/validation/test questions and 38 validation/test recordings (16/22); repeated questions can share source images and voice does not update this LoRA. These are read-from-document explanations, not independent audited counts.
own_workflow_explanation.inputs_outputs: Environment sync consumes the pinned project package specification and chosen extra, producing an installed local toolbox; check_env consumes that interpreter/packages and prints readiness for basic computation, not trained task quality; Jupyter opens a workspace for ordered cells. Skipped-smudge clone obtains source/manifests and LFS pointers rather than binary datasets. Training-asset fetch inputs are selected IDs and a manifest, producing verified expanded files in data/training; Chapter 20 fetch uses its own revision/manifest fingerprint and data/natural-v4, with vision/ocr/voice subfolders. Student release fetch receives its own public manifest and output folder and verifies two small configuration files; official full model weights are a separate later service acquisition. Inference weights/configuration/processors answer questions; resume state additionally preserves optimizer/update state, step, random state and data position.
own_workflow_explanation.skip_or_wait: A reader may skip all installs, datasets, weights, training and publication. Short offline demonstrations do not require the natural-data packs. A Chapter 20 trial may skip all training data and finetuning, but still needs full base and recognizer resources. Run notebook cells and setup commands in order, waiting for each preparation/installation to finish. CPU assistant startup and each speech/chat step have separate waits, and the linked one-machine observations are neither download timings nor universal hardware minima. Matching hashes permit confidence in file identity; ability requires held-out-task assessment.
own_workflow_explanation.symbols_terms: A .venv is a project-specific interpreter/toolbox; --extra chooses a compatible package family; --frozen retains recorded versions; a kernel is the process holding notebook-cell state; SHA-256 is a fingerprint of full bytes; a pointer describes the real LFS object rather than containing the media; fixed revision is a version identity. Seed/configuration enables the small generated worlds to be reproduced. A tokenizer/processor is paired input preparation, which must match the model.
